name: Drinking water
shortNote: 3 L per person, per day
detailNotes: Taiwan: at least 15 mL per kg of body weight, per person, per day. Brunei: 3 L per person, per day.

name: Non-perishable / ready-to-eat food
shortNote: Ready-to-eat: biscuits, instant meals, candy
detailNotes: Biscuits, chocolate, emergency food packs, vacuum-packed instant meals, candies.

name: First aid kit
shortNote: Gauze, iodine, swabs, pain relief, thermometer
detailNotes: Iodine, cotton swabs, gauze, pain-relief patches or ointment, thermometer.

name: Personal medications
shortNote: Daily prescriptions; check expiry dates
detailNotes: Daily prescriptions and standby medication for chronic conditions (e.g. high blood pressure, asthma, diabetes). Note storage method and expiry dates.

name: Face masks (N95 or surgical)
shortNote: Protects against dust, debris and pollutants
detailNotes: Protection from dust, debris and airborne pollutants.

name: Hand sanitiser, wet wipes, tissues
shortNote: Keep hands clean when water is limited

name: Soap & personal hygiene items
shortNote: Include a toothbrush and toothpaste
detailNotes: Indonesia's BPBD DIY guide specifically names a toothbrush and toothpaste.

name: Sanitary pads / diapers
shortNote: Pads, liners; baby diapers if needed
detailNotes: Panty liners; baby diapers if needed.

name: Flashlight or headlamp
shortNote: Store batteries separately to avoid leaks
detailNotes: Store separately from its batteries to avoid leakage or corrosion.

name: Spare batteries
shortNote: Store outside devices to prevent corrosion
detailNotes: Pack extra; don't leave batteries fitted in devices while stored.

name: Portable radio
shortNote: Solar or hand-crank models preferred
detailNotes: Solar- or hand-crank-rechargeable preferred. Singapore's SCDF lists this as optional.

name: Power bank & charging cable
shortNote: Recharge every 2–3 months
detailNotes: Recharge it every 2-3 months so it stays usable. Singapore's SCDF lists this as optional.

name: Copies of ID card & health/insurance card
shortNote: Keep copies in a waterproof folder or phone
detailNotes: Physical copies or digital copies on your phone. Singapore's SCDF specifically recommends a waterproof folder for the physical copies.

name: Small amount of cash
shortNote: Small notes and coins
detailNotes: Small notes/coins, useful for pay phones or vending machines. Singapore's SCDF lists this as optional.

name: List of essential phone numbers
shortNote: Family, utilities, insurer, out-of-area contact
detailNotes: Utility companies, insurer, an out-of-area contact. Taiwan's TFDP frames this as a family emergency contact card.

name: Spare clothing, incl. a raincoat
shortNote: Pack a change of clothes and a raincoat

name: Sturdy, closed-toe shoes
shortNote: For walking over debris and broken glass
detailNotes: For walking over debris or broken glass during evacuation. South Korea's Safe Korea calls these out as "thick indoor shoes."

name: Gloves
shortNote: Cut-resistant and durable
detailNotes: Cut-resistant, durable.

name: Blanket (incl. thermal/emergency blanket)
shortNote: Thermal/emergency blankets pack small

name: Whistle
shortNote: Call for help without shouting
detailNotes: To call for help without shouting, which tires you and risks inhaling dust or smoke.

name: Multi-tool, small knife or scissors
shortNote: One compact tool for cutting and repairs

name: Personal aids: vision, hearing, mobility
shortNote: Spare glasses, hearing aid batteries, cane
detailNotes: Cane, dentures, hearing aids (+ batteries), reading glasses.
teamNote: Listed separately from "Elderly-care items" because these aids are used by people of any age. Same TW/BN sources.

name: Infant supplies
shortNote: Formula, bottles, baby food, diapers, pacifier
detailNotes: Formula, bottles, vacuum-packed/canned baby food, diapers, pacifiers, small toys.

name: Elderly-care items
shortNote: Adult diapers, easy-to-eat senior food
detailNotes: Adult diapers, easy-to-eat/senior-friendly food. (Original source list also included cane, dentures, hearing aids and reading glasses; those now live in "Personal aids: vision, hearing, mobility".)

name: Pet supplies
shortNote: Food, medication, carrier, leash, blanket
detailNotes: Pet food, regular medication, carrier, leash, warm blanket.

name: Sturdy rope
shortNote: From the Philippines' earthquake survival kit
detailNotes: Listed in the Philippines' named earthquake survival kit.

name: Water-resistant matches
shortNote: From the Philippines' earthquake survival kit
detailNotes: Listed in the Philippines' named earthquake survival kit.

name: Fire extinguisher
shortNote: Keep one handy and learn how to use it
detailNotes: Keep one handy and learn how to use it.

name: Baby wrap / carrier
shortNote: Easier than a stroller over debris
detailNotes: A stroller is difficult to use over debris while evacuating with an infant.

name: Head/neck protection (cushion, folded clothing, or a thick book)
shortNote: Shield head and neck while taking cover
detailNotes: To shield your head and neck while taking cover.

name: Portable burner / camp stove
shortNote: For cooking if utilities are cut
detailNotes: For cooking if utilities are cut during prolonged flooding.
